title: Adopt an integrated change into a local checkout before use
purpose: Prevent remote merge proof from being mistaken for local workstation availability. Establish refreshed remote containment, safely update or isolate a local checkout, then execute the newly available validator or launcher from that proven checkout.
triggers: merged change must now run on a workstation
newly merged command is missing locally
remote integration is complete but local adoption is unproved
operator asks why a merged command is not available
inputs: repository path or a bounded repository resolver
integration SHA that introduced the required command or artifact
canonical validator or launcher path resolved from tracked harness metadata
steps: Resolve the actual Git root; do not assume the current shell directory is the repository.
Refresh remote truth with git fetch --all --prune --tags before branch-sensitive conclusions.
Resolve the remote default branch from refs/remotes/origin/HEAD or a provider/symref query; do not assume main.
Prove the integration SHA is an ancestor of the refreshed remote default head with git merge-base --is-ancestor.
Inspect current branch, tracking relationship, HEAD, and git status --short before mutation.
If the current checkout is clean, on the default branch, and behind-only, advance it with git pull --ff-only. If it already contains the integration SHA, do not invent a pull.

If the checkout is dirty, diverged, on separately owned work, or otherwise unsafe to fast-forward, preserve it unchanged and use an isolated worktree or repository-approved equivalent at the refreshed default head for proof.

In the chosen adoption checkout, prove the integration SHA is an ancestor of HEAD and run git ls-files --error-unmatch -- <path> to prove the required validator or launcher is tracked before invoking it.
Run the owning validator first, then run/open the canonical operator artifact only when the requested proof level requires it; propagate every nonzero exit.
Record the adoption checkout path, observed HEAD, integration SHA, containment result, validator command/result, launcher/artifact path, and remaining runtime proof ceiling in the handoff/report.
forbidden: claiming remote merge means a local checkout already has the file
discarding or stashing unrelated dirty work without explicit ownership
executing an untracked or guessed launcher path
outputs: local adoption checkout path and HEAD
canonical launcher or artifact result when executable proof is requested
clean handoff with the next unproved gate
proofCeiling: Proves only the local checkout and commands actually observed in this workflow. Remote integration proof alone never establishes physical workstation adoption or runtime success.
